newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EMERY TO SUPPORT EAST EUROPE GARMENTS TRADE.
newsitem.headline: EMERY TO SUPPORT EAST EUROPE GARMENTS TRADE.

text.p: ~Emery Worldwide~, a part of Consolidated Freightways Transportation Inc , said on Wednesday it planned to add logistics support in central and eastern Europe for the textile industry.

"There are major opportunities for us in the garments and fashion industries in the region -- these manufacturers have been quick to exploit the cost advantages there," Steve Soukup, Emery's division manager for central and eastern Europe, told Reuters by telephone from his office in Zurich.

Emery, which opened its first office in the old East bloc in Budapest in mid-1996, has been working rapidly to integrate its operations in the region into its global network of sector specialists, Soukup said.

It already has automotive and aerospace experts working in Hungary, and it expects to become by 1998 the first freight forwarder there to employ a Japanese national to help serve its Japanese clients, which already include Panasonic, Sony and TDK.

And Emery expects this year to start strengthening ties in central and eastern Europe with its 11 managers world-wide who are dedicated to the clothing business, Soukup said. Focal points include Belarus, Bulgaria, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Ukraine, he added.
"We have plans that will come into play soon," Soukup said. "We are custom-tailoring services to meet the specialised needs of the garments sector."
Details of the plans remain under wraps, but they will involve the introduction of customs-clearing procedures to help apparel exporters and importers, he said.
Emery also plans to start offering special containers with hangers to improve the handling of shipments in the region, he said.

"As clothes come off sewing machines, the manufacturers want to iron and store the garments for transport right away," he said. "We have designed special containers to move garments on hangars that provides more protection for the shippers, and we will start to use them in central and eastern Europe."

The introduction of specialised services reflects Emery's expansion in central and eastern Europe, Soukup said, adding that the company plans to open two subsidiaries in the region by first-quarter 1998.
Emery has boosted its market share for cargo handled among freight forwarders in Hungary to eight percent in first-quarter 1997 from five percent in second-half 1996, Soukup said.
No details were available about the cargo volumes handled, but the growth lifted Emery in the ranking of freight forwarders to the fifth-biggest from the seventh-biggest in the corresponding periods.
Emery also will double its office space in Hungary at the end of August to cope with the growth in business, Soukup said.
